source.title: Classicité de formes modulaires surconvergentes
source.authors: Stéphane Bijakowski, Vincent Pilloni and Benoît Stroh
readSections: The published version, freely served by the Annals site, read in full: 40 pages (pp. 975–1014), SHA-256 13c159cde16c09c98de6b29ed1cf0e293ae78e5dc250399a1ee9203b3601d92c, fetched 29 September 2026. Item locators are the journal's pages. Every recorded mistake was checked on a page image. The paper is in French; statements are translated.

summary: Bijakowski, Pilloni and Stroh extend Coleman's classicality criterion from modular curves to PEL Shimura varieties of type (A) and (C) at Iwahori level, with p unramified and totally split in the reflex field: an overconvergent form that is an eigenform of the Hecke operators U_i at the primes of F0 above p, with non-zero eigenvalues and weight large against their valuations, is classical (Theorem 5.3.1). The proof generalises Buzzard–Kassaei: Fargues's degree measures distance from the ordinary-multiplicative tube, the U_i increase it strictly off integer values (so f extends to X_Iw(1−) by finite slope alone), and on the rest U_i^N is decomposed into good and bad parts over good sequences of opens, where Kassaei series converge under the weight–slope hypothesis and glue modulo p^{A_N}. Lan's Köcher principle and rigid GAGA algebraise the result. The PEL moduli, automorphic bundles, Serre–Tate and GAGA are planned; the paper's machinery joins the proposed Part II HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, and its rigid-geometry, degree, ordinariness and compactification inputs go to AdicSpacesPartII, R07.1, PELModuli M2 and ShimuraCompactifications C5. Seven mistakes are recorded, including a gap in the dimension ≤ 1 case.

items.name: PEL data of type (A) and (C)
items.statement: (B, ⋆) a simple Q-algebra with positive involution, centre F ⊇ F0 = F^⋆ totally real of degree d; type (A) when [F : F0] = 2 (B ⊗_{F0,τ} R ≅ M_n(C) with A ↦ Āᵗ), type (C) when F = F0 and B ⊗_{F,τ} R ≅ M_n(R) with A ↦ Aᵗ. With a non-degenerate anti-hermitian B-module (U_Q, ⟨,⟩), G = Aut_B(U_Q, ⟨,⟩) is the group of B-linear symplectic similitudes; G_R ≅ G(∏_τ U(a_τ, b_τ)) in type (A) and G(∏ Sp_{2a}) in type (C), with a_τ + b_τ = a = dim_Q U_Q/(2nd); h : S → G_R, U^{1,0}, the reflex field E.

items.name: Hypothesis 1.1.1: the good prime p
items.statement: p is unramified in F0 and, in type (A), every place of F0 above p splits in F; B ⊗ Q_p is a product of matrix algebras over unramified extensions; O_B is maximal at p; ⟨,⟩ is perfect at p on the lattice U; and p is totally split in E. Then O_B ⊗ Z_p ≅ ∏_{i=1}^h M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) ⊕ M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) (type (A)) or ∏ M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) (type (C)), for the primes π_1, …, π_h of F0 above p with residue degrees d_i.

items.name: Lemma 1.1.4: signatures are constant above each prime of F0
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 1.1.1, (a_τ, b_τ) = (a_τ′, b_τ′) whenever τ, τ′ lie above the same prime π_i of F0; write (a_i, b_i).

items.name: Morita reduction of O_B ⊗ Z_p-modules
items.statement: M ↦ E_{1,1}·M is an equivalence between M_n(Z_{p^f})-modules and Z_{p^f}-modules; with the idempotents F = (F_i^±) it identifies O_B ⊗ Z_p-modules with modules over ∏ Z_{p^{d_i}} ⊕ Z_{p^{d_i}} (type (A)) or ∏ Z_{p^{d_i}} (type (C)).

items.name: The integral model X without level at p
items.statement: For N ≥ 3 prime to p there is a smooth quasi-projective X over O representing (A, λ, ι, η): A an abelian scheme, λ a prime-to-p polarisation, ι : O_B → End(A) Rosati-compatible with det_{Lie A} = det_{U^{1,0}} (equivalently Lie(A) locally ≅ St ⊗ O_S), and η a symplectic O_B-linear level-N structure lifting étale locally to H_1(A, A_f^p) ≅ U ⊗ A_f^p.

items.name: Serre–Tate: the map to Barsotti–Tate stacks is formally étale
items.statement: The morphism P : X → ∏_i BT^{d_i}_{a_i+b_i} (type (A); ∏_i BT^{d_i,pol}_{a_i} in type (C)) sending A to ∏ G_i, where A[(π_i^+)^∞] = Z^n_{p^{d_i}} ⊗ G_i, is formally étale.

items.name: Barsotti–Tate stacks with Iwahori level and the model X_Iw
items.statement: BT^f_m (height mf, Z_{p^f}-action), BT^{f,pol}_l, their formal variants BT̂^f_{l,m} (dimension lf) and BT̂^{f,pol}_l; an Iwahori structure is a full flag 0 = H_0 ⊂ ··· ⊂ H_m = G[p] of Z_{p^f}-stable finite flat subgroups with H_j of rank p^{fj} (in the polarised case up to H_l, totally isotropic); forgetting it is representable and proper; X_Iw := X ×_{∏BT} ∏BT_Iw, proper over X, parametrising (A, λ, ι, η, H_•).

items.name: Automorphic sheaves ω^κ
items.statement: T = Isom_{O_B ⊗ O_X}(St ⊗ O_X, e*Ω^1_{A/X}) is a torsor under M = ∏ Res(GL_{a_i} × GL_{b_i}) (type (A)) or ∏ Res GL_{a_i} (type (C)); for κ ∈ X(T_M)^+, ω^κ = φ_*O_T[κ′] with κ′ = −w_0κ, the functions on (A, λ, ι, η, (ω_i^±)) transforming by κ′ under the Borel B_M.

items.name: Classical modular forms at Iwahori level
items.statement: Assuming the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1 (Hypothesis 1.4.2, so the Köcher principle applies), a modular form of weight κ on X_Iw × Spec K is a global section of ω^κ.

items.name: Fargues's degree of finite flat group schemes
items.statement: For a finite flat group scheme H over O_K̄, deg(H) ∈ [0, log_p |H|] ([Far10]); a morphism H → H′ that is an isomorphism on generic fibres has deg H ≤ deg H′, with equality iff it is an isomorphism ([Far10, coro. 3]); deg G[p] = dim G for a Barsotti–Tate group G; and the degree of a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level one is an integer ([Pil11, lem. 2.1]).
items.locator: §1.5, p. 987; proofs of Propositions 3.1.1–3.1.2, pp. 992–993 (published version)

items.name: The degree map δ and the ordinary-multiplicative locus
items.statement: δ(G, H_•) = deg(H_l) ∈ [0, fl]; (G, H_•) is ordinary-multiplicative when δ = fl (then G is an extension of an étale BT of height f(m − l) by a multiplicative one and H_l is multiplicative). On the Raynaud generic fibre X^rig_Iw this gives δ : X^rig_Iw → ∏ [0, d_ia_i] and the opens X_Iw(ε) = {δ_i ≥ d_ia_i − ε_i}; X_Iw(0) is the ordinary-multiplicative tube.

items.name: Wedhorn's ordinariness theorem
items.statement: p is totally split in E iff the ordinary locus is dense in X × Spec(O/π) ([Wed99, 1.6.3]); hence X_Iw(0) is non-empty. The ordinary locus of X_Iw × Spec(O/π) is dense if p is totally split in F, and (for p unramified in F) only then.

items.name: Overconvergent modular forms
items.statement: M(X_Iw, κ)† = colim_{ε > 0} H^0(X_Iw(ε), ω^κ), the Q_p-space of overconvergent forms of weight κ.

items.name: Hecke correspondences on Barsotti–Tate stacks
items.statement: C^BT parametrises (G, H_•, L) with L ⊂ G[p] Z_{p^f}-stable and L ⊕ H_l = G[p] (L Lagrangian in the polarised case); p_1 forgets L and p_2 sends it to (G/L, H′_•) with H′_k the image of H_k for k ≤ l and of p^{−1}(H_k ∩ L) for k > l; p_1, p_2 are finite étale and give U : P(BT_Iw(O_K̄)) → P(BT_Iw(O_K̄)).

items.name: Hecke correspondences C_i on X_Iw and the operators U_i on opens
items.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ h, C_i = X_Iw ×_{BT_Iw} C^BT (via p_1, equivalently via p_2) parametrises O_B-stable L ⊂ A[π_i] of type U_i; A/L gets the polarisation x_i·λ for a chosen totally positive x_i ∈ O_{F0} with v_{π_j}(x_i) = δ_{ij} (p·λ when there is one place above p), so U_i is canonical only up to this choice; on admissible opens U_i(V) = p_2(p_1^{−1}(V)).

items.name: The Hecke operators U_i on modular forms
items.statement: Ũ_i = Tr_{p_1} ∘ (π_i^*)^{−1} ∘ p_2^* and U_i = p^{−n_i}Ũ_i with n_i = d_ia_ib_i (type (A)) or d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 (type (C)); explicitly U_i(f)(A, …) = p^{−n_i} Σ_{L of type U_i} f(A/L, …); they act on classical and overconvergent forms and commute.

items.name: Propositions 3.1.1–3.1.3: U does not decrease the degree
items.statement: For x ∈ BT̂^f_{l,m,Iw}(O_K̄) and y ∈ U({x}), δ(y) ≥ δ(x); if equality holds for some y then H_l is a truncated BT of level one and G[p] = H_l ⊕ (another Z_{p^f}-stable truncated BT_1), so δ(x) is an integer; likewise in the polarised case, with both summands totally isotropic.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 and Corollary 3.2.2: dynamics of U_i
items.statement: For integers 0 ≤ n_i ≤ d_ia_i − 1 and reals 0 < η_i ≤ ν_i < 1 there is N with U_i^N(δ_i^{−1}[d_ia_i − n_i − ν_i, d_ia_i]) ⊂ δ_i^{−1}[d_ia_i − n_i − η_i, d_ia_i]; the U_i commute and U_i preserves δ_j for j ≠ i, so (∏ U_i)^N(X_Iw(n + ν)) ⊂ X_Iw(n + η).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2 (Kassaei, Bartenwerfer): bounded sections
items.statement: For a locally free F on an admissible formal scheme with smooth reduced generic fibre and V ⊆ Z^rig quasi-compact, H^0(V, F^rig) ≅ K ⊗_O lim_n H^0(V, F̃^rig/p^n), where F̃^rig is the subsheaf of sections of norm ≤ 1 ([Kas06, lem. 2.3], [Pil11, coro. 5.1]).

items.name: Propositions 4.1.4, 4.1.6, 4.1.7: finite étale maps and strict neighbourhoods
items.statement: A finite étale map of rigid spaces sends opens (quasi-compact opens) to opens (quasi-compact opens) ([Bos09]); strict neighbourhoods are stable under finite intersections and unions; and a finite étale f between quasi-compact rigid spaces sends a strict neighbourhood of U to a strict neighbourhood of f(U) (via [BL93, lem. 5.7, th. 5.2, coro. 5.3] and [AM04, lem. A.1.1]).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.8: a finiteness criterion
items.statement: For f : X → Y finite étale between separated rigid spaces and an open U ⊆ X with U → X quasi-compact, if the geometric fibres of f|_U have constant cardinality then f|_U and f|_{X∖U} are finite étale.

items.name: Identity principle for rigid analytic sections
items.statement: A section of a locally free sheaf on a connected (smooth) rigid space is determined by its restriction to a non-empty open ([Ber96, prop. 0.1.13]); so an extension of an overconvergent form, when it exists, is unique.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.1: continuation to X_Iw(1−)
items.statement: If f ∈ M(X_Iw, κ)† is an eigenform of each U_i with eigenvalue α_i ≠ 0, then f extends canonically to X_Iw(1−) = {δ_i > d_ia_i − 1 for all i}, for every weight κ (only finite slope is used).

items.name: Good sequences of opens and the count N(x, β)
items.statement: A good sequence of a quasi-compact open V is a decreasing sequence (V_k) of quasi-compact opens with V_0 = V and V_k = ∅ for k ≫ 0. On U_γ = δ^{−1}(I_1 × ··· × [0, d_ia_i − 1 + γ] × ··· × I_h), N(x, β) counts y ∈ U_i({x}) with δ_i(y) ≤ d_ia_i − 1 + β, equivalently complements L_0 of type U_i with deg L_0 ≥ n(1 − β) (Remark 4.3.4), and U_k = {N(x, β) ≥ k} is a good sequence of U_γ (Lemma 4.3.6).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7 and Remark 4.3.8: splitting U_i into good and bad parts
items.statement: On U_k ∖ U_{k+1}, N(x, β) = k and U_i = U_i^good ⊔ U_i^bad as finite étale correspondences, U_i^bad being the k complements of degree ≥ n(1 − β); U_i^good lands in δ_i^{−1}(]d_ia_i − 1 + β, d_ia_i]) and U_i^bad in δ_i^{−1}([0, d_ia_i − 1 + β]).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.10: overconvergence of the good sequence
items.statement: For β < β′ < ε and U′_k = {N(x, β′) ≥ k}, U′_k is a strict neighbourhood of U_k for every k ≥ 1.

items.name: Theorem 4.4.1: decomposition of U_i^N
items.statement: For N ≥ 1 and γ, β < ε there are a finite totally ordered S_N and a good sequence (U_k(N))_{k ∈ S_N} of U_γ, of length independent of γ, such that on each U_k(N) ∖ U_{k+1}(N), U_i^N = (⊔_{j<N} U_i^{N−1−j} ∘ T_j) ⊔ T_N with T_j = U^good ∘ (bad)^j, the good operators landing in δ_i^{−1}(]d_ia_i − 1 + β, d_ia_i]) and the bad ones in δ_i^{−1}([0, d_ia_i − 1 + β]); the sequences can be overconverged (β′ > β gives strict neighbourhoods).
items.locator: Theorem 4.4.1, pp. 1000–1001; proof and Lemmas 4.4.2–4.4.4, pp. 1001–1004 (published version)

items.name: Lemma 4.4.5: norm of the bad operators
items.statement: If U_i^bad on V involves only complements L_0 of type U_i with deg L ≥ ν, then ‖U_i^bad‖_V ≤ p^{d_ia_ib_i − ν·inf_j(k_{i,j,a_i} + l_{i,j,b_i})} (type (A)) or p^{d_ia_i(a_i+1)/2 − ν·inf_j k_{i,j,a_i}} (type (C)), κ written as (k_{i,j,1} ≥ ··· ; l_{i,j,1} ≥ ···).

items.name: Hypothesis 4.5.1: the weight–slope condition
items.statement: For every 1 ≤ i ≤ h, inf_j(k_{i,j,a_i} + l_{i,j,b_i}) > v(α_i) + d_ia_ib_i in type (A), and inf_j k_{i,j,a_i} > v(α_i) + d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 in type (C).

items.name: Definition 4.5.2 and Lemma 4.5.3: Kassaei series
items.statement: On V′_k ∖ V_{k+1}, f_{N,k} = α_i^{−1}U^good_{i,k}f + Σ_{j=1}^{N−1} Σ α_i^{−j−1}U^bad ··· U^bad U^good f; with u_0 = p^{n_i + v(α_i) − (1−ε)·inf(weights)} < 1 (Hypothesis 4.5.1), the f_{N,k} are bounded by |α_i^{−1}|p^{n_i}M uniformly in N and k.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.5: Kassaei series agree up to u_0^N
Propositions 4.5.6–4.5.7: gluing the Kassaei series
items.statement: The f_{N,k} glue to g_N ∈ H^0(U, ω̃^κ/p^{A_N}) with A_N → ∞; the g_N form a projective system, so they define g ∈ H^0(U, ω^κ) (by Proposition 4.1.2), which agrees with f on W.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.8: continuation to the whole rigid space
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.5.1 the eigenform f extends to an element of H^0(X^rig_Iw, ω^κ), one direction i at a time.

items.name: Toroidal compactifications at Iwahori level (Lan)
items.statement: For a projective polyhedral cone decomposition S there is a projective X^S_Iw over O whose generic fibre is the toroidal compactification of X_Iw × K and which contains X_Iw as a dense open (using the normality of X_Iw); the forgetful map extends to X^S_Iw → X^S, and ω^κ extends to a locally free sheaf, formally canonical modulo every power of π ([Lan15, déf. 2.7, prop. 2.8, §3, prop. 7.3], [Lan16, rem. 13.12, 16.5], [Lan13, th. 6.4.1.1], [Lan, coro. 5.8–5.9]).

items.name: Normality of the Iwahori-level model
items.statement: X_Iw is normal, by [He13] or by [Str10, prop. 3.1.7.1] together with the flatness of local models ([Gör01] in type (A), [Gör03] in type (C)).
items.note: M4 plans normality and flatness of higher p-level integral models under their actual hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.1: Köcher principle modulo π^n (Lan)
items.statement: If the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1, restriction H^0(X̄^S_Iw × Spec(O/π^n), ω^κ) → H^0(X_Iw × Spec(O/π^n), ω^κ) is an isomorphism for all n ≥ 1 and κ ∈ X^+(T_M) ([Lan15, th. 8.7]).

items.name: Corollaries 5.2.2–5.2.3: formal and rigid Köcher principles
items.statement: Passing to the limit, H^0(X̄^S_Iw, ω^κ) ≅ H^0(X_Iw^∧, ω^κ) on π-adic completions, and on rigid generic fibres H^0((X̄^S_Iw)^rig, ω^κ) ≅ H^0(X^rig_Iw, ω^κ).

items.name: Rigid GAGA (Kiehl)
items.statement: Analytification gives H^0(X̄^S_Iw × Spec K, ω^κ) ≅ H^0((X̄^S_Iw)^rig, ω^κ) ([Kie67]).

items.name: Coleman's classicality theorem on modular curves (Coleman, Kassaei)
items.statement: An overconvergent eigenform of weight k on a modular curve of Iwahori level at p, with U_p-eigenvalue α such that k > 1 + v(α), is classical ([Col96]; Kassaei's proof [Kas06] via Buzzard's dynamics [Buz03]).
items.locator: Introduction, pp. 975–976; proof of Theorem 5.3.1, p. 1011 (published version)

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1: classicality of overconvergent forms of small slope
items.statement: Let X_Iw be a PEL Shimura variety of type (A) or (C) of Iwahori level at p satisfying Hypothesis 1.1.1, κ ∈ X^+(T_M) and f ∈ M(X_Iw, κ)† an eigenform of every U_i (1 ≤ i ≤ h) with non-zero eigenvalue α_i. If κ and the v(α_i) satisfy Hypothesis 4.5.1, f is classical, i.e. in the image of H^0(X_Iw × Spec K, ω^κ) ↪ M(X_Iw, κ)†. (When Hypothesis 1.4.2 fails the paper's argument needs completing, see E6.)

items.name: Explicit weight–slope conditions
items.statement: For the Siegel variety of GSp_{2g} over a totally real F of degree d with p inert, the condition is inf_σ k_{σ,g} > v(α) + dg(g + 1)/2; for a unitary group of signature (a, b) over a CM field F with p inert in F0 and split in F, it is inf_σ(k_{σ,a} + l_{σ,b}) > v(α) + dab.
items.locator: Remark after the main theorem, p. 977 (published version)

routes.reason: R2 owns admissible formal schemes, blow-ups and generic fibres, and R3 coherent sheaves, finite étale traces and Kiehl-type finiteness. The paper's general rigid-geometry inputs — the Kassaei–Bartenwerfer description of sections by bounded sections, images of opens and strict neighbourhoods under finite étale maps (through Bosch–Lütkebohmert flattening), the finiteness criterion 4.1.8 and the identity principle — are statements about those objects, used by any analytic-continuation argument.

R07.1 owns finite flat group schemes over mixed-characteristic bases; Fargues's degree and its monotonicity under generic isomorphisms extend that layer and are the quantity the whole dynamics is measured in.

M2 owns the smooth PEL model at a good prime; Wedhorn's theorem that the ordinary locus of its special fibre is dense exactly when p splits completely in the reflex field is a statement about that model.

C5 owns integral PEL compactifications, including the higher p-level normalisations; Lan's toroidal compactifications of the Iwahori-level model, the extension of automorphic sheaves and Lan's Köcher principle modulo π^n are the results of that layer the paper consumes.

routes.title: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology
routes.brief: This route joins the proposal of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory made from PAPER-PILLONI-20 and joined by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (same id, parent, title and area); the design job merges its brief with theirs. Bijakowski–Pilloni–Stroh (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 975–1014) supply the degree-0 Coleman theory for PEL Shimura varieties of type (A) and (C) at Iwahori level with p unramified and split in the reflex field: Theorem 5.3.1, an overconvergent eigenform of every U_i with non-zero eigenvalues and weight large against the slopes (Hypothesis 4.5.1: inf(k + l) > v(α_i) + d_ia_ib_i in type (A), inf k > v(α_i) + d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 in type (C)) is classical. Build, in order: Barsotti–Tate stacks with Iwahori level and X_Iw; Fargues's degree map δ and the ordinary-multiplicative tube; overconvergent forms; the Hecke correspondences U_i normalised by p^{−n_i}; the dynamics (Propositions 3.1.1–3.2.2); continuation to X_Iw(1−) by finite slope alone; the good/bad decomposition of U_i^N over good sequences of opens (§§4.3–4.4) with the norm bound of Lemma 4.4.5; Kassaei series and their gluing modulo p^{A_N} (§4.5); and the formal and rigid Köcher principles with GAGA to algebraise. Keep the case where the symmetric space has dimension ≤ 1 explicit (PAPER-BIJAKOWSKI-PILLONI-STROH-16/E6): Coleman–Kassaei covers only the modular curve. Import PEL moduli (PELModuli M0, M2, M4), Serre–Tate (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4), automorphic bundles and classical forms (AutomorphicBundles B2, B4), Fargues's degree (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1), rigid geometry and GAGA (AdicSpacesPartII R1–R3), Wedhorn's theorem (PELModuli M2) and Lan's compactifications and Köcher principle (ShimuraCompactifications C5). The higher Coleman theory of the joined briefs recovers this degree-0 statement for GSp_{2g}; the design should record the comparison rather than build two classicality theorems for the same group.
routes.reason: Classicality of small-slope overconvergent forms is Coleman theory for coherent cohomology in degree 0, which is exactly the direction of the proposed HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; PadicFamilies itself stops at modular curves and totally real fields in one degree, and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms builds coefficient sheaves, not classicality.

sourceIssues.printed: The source cites [Gro71, V, coro. 3.5] to claim U → Y is both open and closed, and deduces that X∖U → Y is also finite étale.
sourceIssues.correction: the open immersion U → X is open and closed (U → X is a morphism of finite étale Y-spaces), so X∖U → Y is finite étale
sourceIssues.reason: That U → Y is open and closed does not give the conclusion; what is needed, and what SGA 1 V 3.5 gives, is that U is a union of connected components of X.

sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that failure of Hypothesis 1.4.2 for G makes its symmetric space the Poincaré half-plane, and that [Col96] or [Kas06] then proves the theorem.
sourceIssues.correction: When the symmetric space has dimension ≤ 1 the variety need not be a modular curve: type (C) with B an indefinite quaternion algebra over Q (n = 2) gives Shimura curves, type (A) with Σ_τ a_τb_τ = 1 gives unitary curves, and Σ a_τb_τ = 0 gives finite sets. For compact curves the continuation of §4 together with GAGA on the proper X_Iw proves the theorem; non-compact unitary curves need the cusp analysis of Remark 5.3.2 or a comparison with modular curves.
sourceIssues.reason: [Col96] and [Kas06] treat the modular curve (GL_2 over Q). Theorem 5.3.1 assumes only Hypothesis 1.1.1, which allows those other PEL data, and Definition 1.4.3 relies on Hypothesis 1.4.2 to ignore cusps.

sourceIssues.printed: The source assumes the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1, then recasts this, using §1.1 notation, as d > 1 or a_1 > 1 if d = 1.
sourceIssues.correction: The dimension is Σ_τ a_τb_τ in type (A) and d·a(a + 1)/2 in type (C); the reformulation is right in type (C) only.
sourceIssues.reason: In type (A), U(1, 2) over an imaginary quadratic field (d = 1, a_1 = 1) has a 2-dimensional symmetric space, and d = 2 with signatures (1, 1) and (0, 2) (p split in F0) gives dimension 1 although d > 1. Proposition 5.2.1 uses the dimension condition itself (Lan's theorem), so nothing downstream depends on the reformulation.
